title: Clinical Technology Feasibility Assessment on CRM Platform
summary: Assessment of building clinical trial technology capabilities on a CRM platform, including key entity analysis, data model mapping, and gap identification.

findings.key_clinical_entities: Clinical technology requires managing: Sites, Investigators (HCPs with credentials), Trials (study protocols), Agreements/Invoices/Budgets, and Payments (investigator compensation and transparency).
findings.data_model_approach: Maps clinical entities to platform constructs: Sites as Account records with clinical record types, Investigators as Contact/HCP records, Trials as custom objects with study protocol metadata.
findings.platform_capabilities_applicable: Capabilities transferring from commercial CRM: territory management (study site alignment), visit tracking (monitor-site interactions), consent management (study consent), mobile offline sync (field monitor data capture).
findings.identified_gaps: Gaps requiring custom dev or integration: IRT for randomization, EDC for case report forms, eTMF for document management, safety database integration for adverse event reporting.
findings.clinical_persona_value: A clinical CRM persona applies commercial engagement patterns (360 view, next-best-action) to site engagement, orchestrating interactions to optimize enrollment and investigator satisfaction.
findings.integration_architecture: Requires integration with CTMS, IRT, EDC, safety systems, and financial systems for investigator payments. APIs and middleware are essential.

source: Clinical technology feasibility analysis assessing CRM platform capabilities for clinical trial operations
